contentBlocks.text: ਮੈਂ ਪਾਣੀ ਪੀਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ! (Main paani peenda haan! - I drink water!) Yesterday your sentences said WHO did something. Today let's grow them by adding WHAT.

Remember paani (water) from last year? Now we can build a bigger sentence: ਮੈਂ ਪਾਣੀ ਪੀਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ (main paani peenda haan, I drink water). The pattern grows to: who + what + action. Try building one more: use ghar (home) with the verb jaana (to go) — main ghar jaanda haan (I go home).
Your sentences are getting bigger and more detailed! Tomorrow we'll use everything you've learned to read a short story.

objectives: Build a 'who + what + action' sentence, combining a subject, an object, and a verb
Reuse last year's family/home vocabulary (paani, ghar) in a new sentence-building context
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review paani and ghar from last year.
2. Introduce the new verb jaana (to go).
3. Model main paani peenda haan and main ghar jaanda haan together.
4. Practice building 1-2 more sentences combining last year's vocabulary with this week's verbs.
5. Move to the worksheet: build each sentence using the given word and verb.
6. Close by having the child say their favorite new sentence out loud.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just one complete sentence (main paani peenda haan) rather than building several
Ready for more: challenge the child to build a sentence using a word not explicitly given, from memory
For a child who enjoys drawing, have them illustrate their sentence to reinforce meaning
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a sentence-building activity — check that the child correctly combines main, an object word, and a verb into a complete sentence.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Growing sentences with an object is the natural next step in the Grade 2 Punjabi course's sentence-construction sequence, building directly on yesterday's subject+verb pattern.

generationData.instructions: Build a sentence using each word and verb given.

prompts.prompt: Build a sentence using paani (water) and peena (to drink).
Build a sentence using ghar (home) and jaana (to go).
